_README: FIXTURE 5 — THE SABOTAGED ONTOLOGY (MASTER_PIPELINE SS11.3 fixture 3). MUST BE CAUGHT
BY THE CONTROL PROBE, NOT BY A VIOLATION.
SS11.3 asks for 'a lint whose regex is deliberately broken — the control probe must catch
it.' In seed-lint the equivalent sabotage is not a regex: Rules A and B are driven
entirely by the ontology's synonyms[] and constituents[] lists. Empty those and the
rules go silent. THE LINT THEN REPORTS 'no violations' ON THE REAL DEMAND MAP — a
THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. From our own record: a banned-word scan on this machine
returned '0 hits — a false negative'; the [[:<:]] word-boundary syntax silently fails
under ugrep. The control word 'ayurveda' ALSO returned 0, WHICH IS WHAT EXPOSED IT.
Without that control word the scan would have been believed.
A LINT RETURNING ZERO BECAUSE ITS MATCHER SILENTLY DIED IS FAILURE #2 LIVING INSIDE THE
GATE BUILT TO PREVENT FAILURE #2 — an implausible zero, believed, reported as PASS.
EXPECTED: seed-lint verdict FAIL with control_probes_ok === false, and it must fail
EVEN THOUGH violations.length === 0. If a sabotaged ontology yields PASS, the SX rule
is not implemented and every clean run in this repo is worthless.
SABOTAGE APPLIED: every synonyms[] and constituents[] list emptied. Nothing else touched.
